response.passage: Rohan and Priya were designing garden plots for their school project. Rohan built a square plot with a side of 4 meters, while Priya built a rectangular plot with a length of 6 meters and a width of 2 meters. Rohan calculated that both plots have a perimeter of 16 meters, so he assumed they must also have the same area. However, when they calculated the actual space inside, Rohan’s square had an area of 16 square meters, while Priya’s rectangle had an area of only 12 square meters. This proved that shapes with identical perimeters do not necessarily enclose the same amount of area. Next, they decided to cover their plots with soil. Rohan needed to convert his measurement of 1 square meter into square centimeters to buy the right amount of fertilizer. He initially thought it was 100 square centimeters, but he realized that since 1 meter equals 100 centimeters, 1 square meter is actually 10,000 square centimeters. By multiplying 100 by 100, he corrected his mistake and bought the correct quantity. They learned that perimeter and area are independent properties, and unit conversions for area require squaring the conversion factor of the length.
response.summary: The passage explains that shapes with equal perimeters can have different areas. It also clarifies that converting square meters to square centimeters requires multiplying by 10,000 instead of 100.
